blogs.title: The High-Amylase Trap: Diagnosing Pancreatopleural Fistula in Uncomplicated Respiratory Workups
blogs.description: An exploration of the diagnostic limitations when a patient presents with recurrent pleural effusions and respiratory distress. This post focuses on the pivotal role of pleural fluid amylase levels (specifically the >1000 U/L threshold noted in our case) in distinguishing Pancreatopleural Fistula (PPF) from common differentials like Tuberculosis (elevated ADA), Malignancy, and simple empyema. We discuss how failing to identify the pancreas as the source before ordering an extensive pulmonary workup leads to diagnostic delay.

blogs.title: The Pulmonary Mask: Why Trauma History Matters in Recurrent Pleural Effusions
blogs.description: This post analyzes the clinical presentation of PPF as a thoracic pathology despite its abdominal origin. Using the case of a child with 'dark red' fluid and a missed bicycle handle trauma, we discuss the importance of forearm trauma histories in subacute respiratory presentations. We examine the 'Pulmonary Mask' phenomenon where chest symptoms override abdominal signs, and discuss how to force a re-evaluation of history in patients undergoing repeated thoracentesis.

blogs.title: Imaging the Fistula: When CT Chest is Not Enough and Why MRCP is Gold
blogs.description: A technical discussion on the diagnostic imaging hierarchy for suspected Pancreatopleural Fistulas. We compare the sensitivity of standard CT scans (often missing the fistulous tract) against the 70-80% sensitivity of MRCP. The post highlights the case findings where CT suggested the collection but MRCP confirmed the anatomical tracking through the oesophageal hiatus, and when ERCP remains the gold standard for surgical planning versus MRCP for non-invasive diagnosis.

blogs.title: NPO, Nutrition, and Octreotide: The Conservative Management of Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: A review of first-line medical therapy for PPF, focusing on the conservative regimen described in the case report. We detail the administration of octreotide (30 µg/kg/day), total parenteral nutrition (TPN) for bowel rest, and pancreatic enzyme replacement. We analyze the success rate timeline (fluid drainage reduction over 10 days) versus the uncertain long-term success rates of conservative management in paediatric literature (12%), helping clinicians navigate when to escalate to ERCP or surgery.

blogs.title: Pediatric vs. Adult PPF: Trauma and Genetics vs. Alcohol
blogs.description: This post contextualizes PPF by contrasting the etiology in adults versus children. While alcohol accounts for the vast majority of adult cases (up to 99% in Japanese cohorts), paediatric PPF is driven by blunt abdominal trauma (32% in the case review) or genetic mutations (PRSS1, SPINK1). We discuss why clinicians must ask different questions for a child presenting with PPF compared to an adult, and the implications of screening family history for hereditary pancreatitis in this rare abdominal condition.
